lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Education appears before Experience even though work history is the stronger evidence of professional direction.
items.because: The ordering delays the strongest evidence for a reader.

items.says: The period from May 2021 to April 2022 is unexplained.
“Update speed” does not identify the measure or comparison behind the 60% gain.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what improved or interpret the size of the gain.

items.says: The 400-test figure reports testing activity but not its effect.
items.because: It does not show whether the rig caught regressions, reduced manual work, or improved release confidence.

items.says: “Which found the root cause” could refer to the flash or saved data rather than the logger or its use.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz does not capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The 8 kHz sample rate has a 4 kHz Nyquist frequency, below the signal’s frequency.

items.says: The sampling clause describes an intended capability but not its effect in use.
Declaring the shared counter volatile does not fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not guarantee atomic access or synchronization between the interrupt handler and main loop.

items.says: The claim that the race condition was fixed gives no effect on the system.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what operational problem the change resolved.

items.says: Repeating “the counter” makes the explanation unnecessarily repetitive.
“Rewrote the motor-controller firmware” does not identify the technical change behind the improvements.
items.because: A reader cannot see the embedded engineering approach that drove the results.

items.says: The 60% reduction in field motor faults has no baseline or comparison period.
items.because: A reader cannot gauge the operational scale of the reduction.

items.says: The strongest Voltline bullet is placed last rather than first.
items.because: A scanning reader encounters the clearest combination of scale and measured results later.

items.says: “Automated end-of-line tests” does not show what test step or automation element was implemented.
The return-rate reduction appears only at the end of the bullet.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the result after the failure context and diagnosis.

items.says: “Wrote the calibration procedure” does not indicate what calibration approach or check it specified.
The eight-board capacity does not show what design feature enabled simultaneous checks.
“IoT solution” does not say what was built or how.
items.because: The bullet gives no concrete technical detail that shows the contribution or skill.

items.says: The claim that the project “redefines sustainable environmental sensing” gives no concrete outcome or evidence of impact.
items.because: Without a result or comparison, its impact is difficult to assess and the promotional phrasing leaves the work unclear.

items.says: The strongest weather-station bullet is not the opening one.
items.because: Its quantified current reduction and explanation would put direct evidence before a scanning reader.

items.says: The school’s adoption shows how many stations were built but not what they enabled.
“Openly” is vague and redundant with “published.”
“Robot fleet’s motor controllers” misdescribes work under a Formula Student electric-car project.
items.because: Work on the student race car’s motor controller does not establish work for a robot fleet.

items.because: The broad terms hide the work performed and give no clear example of technical skill.

items.says: The bullet gives no outcome or evidence of what the work changed.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the contribution accomplished or how successful it was.
